reason: The mechanism exposes a native Java interface to potentially untrusted web content via addJavascriptInterface, which is a known security risk allowing JavaScript to invoke arbitrary Java methods, leading to possible code execution or data leakage.
summary: Evidence indicates that using addJavascriptInterface with untrusted or interceptable HTML/JS can enable attackers to execute arbitrary code via the exposed interface, violating safe usage guidelines.

citations.title: Android WebView addJavascriptInterface Security Risks | PTKD Journal
citations.snippet: addJavascriptInterface bridges JavaScript to a native object, and its risk depends on your API level and what content the WebView loads. Per the Android WebView reference, apps targeting API 17 and above only expose methods marked @JavascriptInterface, which closed the original reflection-to-RCE exploit (CVE-2012-6636) that affected older versions.
